1. Heard Shri Ganapati M.Bhat, learned counsel for the petitioner and Shri Praveena Y.
Devareddiyavara, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 - State.

Brief facts of the case are as under:
2. It is the case of the prosecution that, the petitioner said to have had love affair with the victim and he is stated to have abducted the victim on 11.04.2023.
A complaint came to be lodged by the father of the victim on 12.04.2023 regarding the missing of his daughter.
The Police have registered a case in Crime No.35/2023 for the offence under Section 363 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC') and conducted the investigation.

During investigation, they found that the petitioner herein abducted and confined the victim in Kadra at his relative's house for a period of one month and committed sexual intercourse on several occasions and after the petitioner came to know that a case has been registered against him for abduction and kidnapping, he has sent the victim to her native.
Soon after she went to her native, she went to the police station and made confession regarding her missing and also NC: 2023:KHC-D:13297 narrated the incident before the jurisdictional police.

The jurisdictional police after recording the statement, conducted the investigation and submitted the charge sheet for the offence under Sections 363, 376, 506 of IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short 'POCSO Act').

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that, the petitioner is innocent of the alleged offences and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
He was working as a coolie and resident of Janatha Colony, Taragoda village, Sirsi Taluk.
He further submitted that both the petitioner and victim are the residents of same village and both have decided to marry each other.
Therefore, on the pretext of she having completed her 18 years, the petitioner went along with her to his relative's house and stayed for one month and he was intending to marry her.
By that time, he came to know that a case has been registered against him, the petitioner sent her back to her native.
However, the police have registered a case against the petitioner which is false and unimaginable.
It is further submitted that, in the event of his release on bail, he is ready to abide all the conditions that would be imposed by NC: 2023:KHC-D:13297 this Court.

Petitioner is in judicial custody since Yogesh S/O. Dadappa Bhovivaddar vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149216927/
2 18.05.2023.

entities.text: Yogesh S/O. Dadappa Bhovivaddar vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.
4. Per contra, Shri Praveena Y. Devareddiyavara, the learned High Court Government Pleader orally objected and opposed the bail application and submitted that the offence is heinous in nature.
The age of the victim is 16 years 7 months as on the date of the alleged incident.

She was abducted and confined in the room without giving basic necessities and also not allowed her to contact any of her relatives and the petitioner committed sexual intercourse on several occasions, which is not only heinous in nature, but, also scar on her future life.
If the petitioner is enlarged on bail, there may be chances of absconding from the case.
Therefore, it is appropriate to dismiss the petition.
Making such submission, the learned HCGP prays to dismiss petition.

5. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments made in the charge sheet and also statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., it is noticed that the statement of the victim recorded NC: 2023:KHC-D:13297 before the Magistrate contains some contradictions and some improvements.

Moreover, the learned counsel for the petitioner has stated that, the actual age of the victim was not known to the petitioner and the petitioner was told that she had completed 18 years, hence, he decided to marry her.
Therefore, without adverting to the merit of the case, on careful reading of the statement of the victim, it makes it clear that that the petitioner may be released on bail.

6. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Special Case No.74/2023 (Crime No.35/2023 of Sirsi Rural Police Station) pending on the file of Court of the Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-1, U.K., Karwar (Special Court for trial of cases filed under POCSO Act), on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, subject to the following conditions:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:13297 a) The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses nor hamper the proceedings of the Court.

entities.text: Court of the Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-1, U.K., Karwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: b) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing without fail.
In case, if the petitioner violates any of the bail conditions as stated above, the prosecution will be at liberty to seek for cancellation of bail.
